label: Aristotle, Metaphysics II.1, 993b30-31: As each thing stands in respect of being, so it stands in…
interpretation: The chapter's closing inference (ὥσθʼ ἕκαστον ὡς ἔχει τοῦ εἶναι, οὕτω καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας), read as a correspondence of standing said of things: having truth goes with having being, and being more true with being more a being. 'True' is the truth of things, as the context requires: the principles are cause of the posterior things' being true and, being always, are always most true (993b26-30); this is the sense Aquinas gives verum in the quarta via (DEF-ONTOLOGICAL-TRUTH), which cites this sentence. The biconditionals follow the proportional 'as ... so'; no measure, total order or universal comparability is read in. Rejected strengthening: an identity of truth with being. Unformalized narrower reading: the correspondence holds only for the principles of the eternal beings and what they cause, the immediate subject of 993b26-30; under it this claim would overstate the sentence, and a sibling claim should be added if that reading is defended.
